summary: All six findings confirmed; four fixes are corrected. /1: route 1 depends on routes 2 and 6 with neither encoded, and since make_queue groups Part IIs by parent the route ids no longer name design jobs; the ordering belongs on whichever job designs Macaulayfication (the Scheme Part II job designs only its first continuation), the supplier should be named by title, id and extraction route, and reserved ids are the maintainer's. /2: AS.1 does not plan Noetherian dualizing complexes or local duality, and the IKM-24 rejection leaves the owner open; move items 39, 79, 80 to R03.3 (which already has local cohomology, Matlis duality, and via CG-18 canonical modules), leaving route 5 with item 52 — no joint cross-paper move is needed. /3: split item 16; the sheaf-level notions go to SF.0 (route 3), not route 1, since accepted routes already use them in SF.0/SF.2. /4: state EGA IV₂ 7.4.4 in ring form on route 4 for R03.3, where accepted routes already put special cases, not on route 1. /5: confirmed as written. /6: the 'published' file is the author's 28 July 2020 manuscript; REQUESTS.md is generated, so leave a maintainer note instead of editing it.

sources.citation: Author's final manuscript dated 28 July 2020 (hash matches the extraction's record). The Duke Math. J. 170 (2021) text was not readable: Project Euclid returned a bot-block page.

findings.reason: Confirmed. I checked each part at its evidence. (1) The dependency is real. In the TeX, the proof of Proposition 4.4 uses Theorem 3.14 (label Kaw-blowup) to make Bl_J(M) Cohen–Macaulay, Lemma 3.6 (Ann-ref) for the stalks of the ideals I_M and I_{M,m}, the module blowups of §3.13, and Lemma 4.3 (GLL-input) to choose f_m. Those are items 48–49, 40, 47 and 53, which sit in routes 2 and 6, while Proposition 4.4 (items 54–55) sits in route 1. (2) The encoding is missing. Route 1's prerequisites name neither sibling. Its brief says it 'starts after … its sibling … (KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps)' and imports the avoidance lemma 'from SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartIIArithmeticPresentation'. The route schema of PROTOCOL §16 has no prerequisites field, and make_queue does not read it, but other extractions list sibling Part II ids there, so adding one follows precedent. (3) The queue behaves as the finding says. paper_designs (make_queue.py ll. 413–448, added in commit 7685a59f on 28 September, after the review of 24 September) groups every part-ii route by parent (l. 423). It gives each member only an excerpt and the pointer 'the route to <roadmap>'. I re-ran the grouping read-only on the accepted routes. SchemeAndStackFoundations now has 10 continuations, not 9: RT-PAPER-BAKKER-TSIMERMAN-16/4 has since added the complex-surface contractions. Both CS-21 routes 1 and 6 are among them. The first is Česnavičius–Scholze flat cohomology. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra has one continuation, the Kawasaki route. queue.json has DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII at order 31 and DESIGN-DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII at order 146, both priority 1 and both with after = []. The line numbers have moved slightly since the swarm intake commit. lane.py claims jobs by (priority, order), so the local lane takes the consumer's job first. Issues #3361 and #3476 are both open and state:available. No roadmap will carry the ids MacaulayficationOfNoetherianSchemes, KawasakiCohenMacaulayBlowingUps or SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartIIArithmeticPresentation. (4) The review's make_queue sentence ('one brief per shared design id, the later paper wins') was true when it was written: add() overwrote the prompt of a repeated id. It has been false since 7685a59f. Refinements to the fix. (a) Name the supplier robustly. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII is right today, but it is fragile. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 route 1 is another Part II of the same parent (CongruenceModulesHigherCodimension), currently rejected pending revision. It comes earlier in papers.json (no. 85 against 213). If it is accepted, it becomes 'the first' continuation, and the Kawasaki direction could be pushed into a restructure proposal. So route 1's brief should name the supplier by title and id, 'Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching, Part II (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII)'. It should also say that the job DESIGN-DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII plans it from route 2 of this extraction. The brief should name the avoidance lemma as 'the arithmetic-presentation continuation of Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations, Part II (route 6 here and route 13 of PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23, both in DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII)'. Also add DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII to route 1's prerequisites. (b) Delete the make_queue sentence from route 6's reason. Optionally cut route 6's brief to its own addition, the Noetherian projective case of avoidance. Each member is now listed separately, so the copy of BHATT-ETAL-23's brief only duplicates an entry. Leave review.json and the review report as dated records. (c) For the maintainer, the most likely outcome is different from the one the fix assumes. DESIGN-SchemeAndStackFoundationsPartII is told to 'plan the first here and record a restructure proposal for the rest'. The first is flat cohomology, so Macaulayfication will most likely become a restructure proposal, not part of that job. Making the whole 10-continuation job wait for the commutative Part II would hold back unrelated directions. The ordering should instead be put on whichever job actually designs the Macaulayfication direction, and the restructure proposal should carry both imports, Kawasaki and avoidance. (d) The reserved-ids alternative is the maintainer's to apply. research/blueprint/reserved-ids.json is generated from the RESERVED table in make_queue.py, and design jobs are told not to edit reserved ids. So the ids for Proposition 3.11, §3.13 and Theorem 3.14 must be added there, with job DESIGN-DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebraPartII. Medium is the right severity.

Confirmed. (1) AS.1 does not plan these items. Its text in research/blueprint/roadmaps/AnalyticStacks.json covers locally compact Hausdorff spaces, the quasi-coherent formalism on derived schemes over animated rings, Grothendieck–Serre duality for proper smooth maps, and D-modules and de Rham stacks. Its requires are AS.0, SA.0 (light condensed anima), E1, E5:animation, SF.1 and DD.2. Nothing in it covers a dualizing complex of a Noetherian ring, D^b_coh duality, normalisation or local duality, and item 39's note concedes this. (2) What the paper uses is purely ring-level. I read §3.5 and Lemma 3.6 in the TeX: Stacks 0A7B–0A7I, 0DW7, 0AWS, 0A7Z and 0A7U, plus local duality in the form of Hartshorne RD V 6.2 / Schenzel 1.3.4, for a Noetherian local ring. Route 2 imports items 39, 79 and 80 from AS.1 and lists AnalyticStacks among its prerequisites. At stage level, the commutative Part II therefore sits downstream of AS.0, SA.0, E1, E5:animation and DD.2, none of which the mathematics needs. Mathlib's triangulated DerivedCategory and localCohomology are enough for the definitions. The dependency-weight argument holds. (3) The IKM-24 rejection is misread. The route 3 verdict says the duality package is 'not explicitly in the named stage contracts'. Gap G2 in REV-PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24.md says 'Establish the unique generic owner and precise extension before route 3 can be activated', and warns that adjacent geometric suppliers are 'not automatically this ring theorem'. The review never names AS.1. IKM route 3's own reason had AS.1's scheme-level complex 'import this local version'. Since AS.1's contract covers the ring-level theory no better than R03.3's, the rejection does not confirm AS.1. (4) R03.3 is the right recommendation, and the case is stronger than the finding says. This extraction's route 4 already gives R03.3 local cohomology (item 76) and the injective hull with Matlis duality (item 78), which are the inputs of local duality. The accepted route 4 of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 gives R03.3 the canonical module of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring, Gorenstein theory and Eisenbud 21.15, and calls R03.3 'the owner of depth, Cohen–Macaulay and Gorenstein theory'. The canonical module is the Cohen–Macaulay case of a normalized dualizing complex (Stacks 0AWS, which item 80 states). No other atlas stage plans coherent ring duality. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves and the CS-24 Part II item 047 plan étale dualizing complexes. StableReduction Layer 2 plans the relative dualizing sheaf of CM curves. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration LI.1 only takes an inventory of dualizing modules. Correction to the fix: nothing needs to 'move together'. The AS.1 items of HACON-WITASZEK-23 route 5 (dualizing, derived-local), BHATT-ETAL-23 route 5 (dualizing, local-duality-a/b, top-duality) and ZAVYALOV-25 route 2 are all scheme-level: normalized dualizing complexes on excellent schemes, finite traces, duality for schemes proper over a complete local base, and f^!. None of them is the ring-level theory of items 39, 79 and 80. They, and item 52, can stay with the scheme-level owner and import the ring-level items. Route 5's reason overstates when it says those routes made AS.1 'the single owner of dualizing complexes of Noetherian rings and schemes'; it should say scheme-level adapters. The right fix follows from this. Because no other paper's items have to move, the fixer can make the move now, without waiting for a joint decision. 1. Move items 39, 79 and 80 to route 4 (R03.3). Its reason should state the extension explicitly ('dualizing complexes of Noetherian rings, their normalisation, localisation and quotients, existence over complete local rings, the Cohen–Macaulay criteria and local duality'), which meets G2. 2. Rewrite route 5 to carry item 52 alone, drop the IKM sentence, and add a note that the scheme-level owner imports the ring-level items from R03.3. AS.1's requires do not yet include R03.3, although BHATT-ETAL-23 route 5 already imports Matlis duality from it. 3. In route 2, rewrite the brief's AS.1 import as an R03.3 import, and drop AnalyticStacks from its prerequisites. 4. In route 1's brief, change 'AS.1 for dualizing complexes … (items 39, 52, 79, 80)' to R03.3 for 39, 79 and 80 and AS.1 for 52. 5. Update the notes of items 39, 79, 80 and 81. If the lead prefers not to override the review's deferral, the minimum is to correct the IKM sentence and the 'single owner' claim, and to record R03.3 as the recommended owner for the maintainer. Medium is the right severity: it changes where a piece of foundational mathematics is planned and what a commutative roadmap depends on.

The gap is real. I read the §1.14 source at the TeX: the support of a coherent module is the closed subscheme cut out by its annihilator; (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay coherent modules are defined stalkwise; and a scheme is (S_n) or Cohen–Macaulay when O_X is. That last predicate is the conclusion of Theorem 1.6. Item 16 is marked planned in R03.3 and SF.0, but neither layer plans these notions. R03.3 speaks only of finite modules over rings. SF.0 constructs only schemes and quasi-coherent modules. The (S_k) precedent the note cites, PAPER-HACON-WITASZEK-23/cm-depth, is stated 'for finite modules over Noetherian local rings'. R03.3's accepted decomposition has no Cohen–Macaulay node, and its coverage lists Cohen–Macaulay modules as not yet read. Route 1's brief imports 'the Serre conditions' from R03.3. Its 'Construct here' paragraph names the (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay loci, the (S_1)-ification and (S_n)-quasi-excellence, but never the sheaf-level predicates. So the note's sentence 'route 1 states [it] as an adapter' is false, and item 16 is only half planned. Mathlib at 082e2d3 and Tau Ceti at f790474 have no depth and no Cohen–Macaulay predicate. The fix needs one change: the owner. Route 1 is the wrong owner, because accepted routes already send consumers of this predicate into SchemeAndStackFoundations itself. PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-20/T58 (codimension-two extension of Cohen–Macaulay sheaves; route 6 to SF.0) is accepted, and so is PAPER-PILLONI-20 route 24 (the SGA 2 III §3 depth statement for a locally free sheaf on a Cohen–Macaulay scheme, to SF.2). BHATT-ETAL-23/plus-cm and HACON-WITASZEK-23/total-cm also need Cohen–Macaulay schemes, in the mixed-characteristic Part II. A Part II starts after its parent, so defining the predicate in route 1 would make SF.0 and SF.2 depend on their own Part II. The right fix is to split item 16. The module-level part (depth, (S_k), Cohen–Macaulay modules) stays planned in R03.3. The sheaf-level part becomes a missing item on the existing source route 3, into SF.0. That item states: Supp(𝓜) as the closed subscheme of Ann_{O_X}(𝓜); stalkwise (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay coherent modules, with the E4 quantifier over x ∈ Supp(𝓜); the characterisation of (S_1) by the absence of embedded associated primes (EGA IV₂ 5.7.5); and (S_n) and Cohen–Macaulay locally Noetherian schemes. Route 1 keeps item 26's loci and imports these definitions from SF.0. Item 16's note should then name SF.0 (route 3) as owner of the sheaf-level part.

The missing theorem is real, but the fix names the wrong owner. Uses in the TeX: Remark 1.5 (l. 789) cites EGA IV₂ 7.4.4 with 7.3.8. The proof of Proposition 2.7 (l. 1016) says 'Since X̃ inherits quasi-excellence', which is the regular case (EGA IV₂ 7.8.3(ii)) for the finite normalisation. §2.10 (l. 1087) says the same for (S_n). The ascent is also used without citation in the proof of Lemma 2.11 (l. 1151), Corollary 2.14 (l. 1198) and Proposition 5.5 (l. 1998). Corollaries 1.8 and 1.11 apply Remark 1.5 to finite-type schemes over a base that is CM-excellent but possibly not excellent, such as a Dedekind scheme. So the finite-type case for P = Cohen–Macaulay is genuinely needed. For finite morphisms the ascent is elementary, since each formal fibre upstairs is a direct factor of a finite-field-extension base change of one downstairs. The finite-type case is the substantial part of 7.4.4. On the items: 6 and 28 state the CM and (S_n) consequences, and route 1's brief constructs 'their stability under localisation and finite type'. So those consequences have a supplier, but the theorem behind them has no item. The regular case has neither: item 1 gives only the definitions and the openness of Reg(X), and item 25 asserts 'X̃ is excellent' with no input for it. No stage text, proposed roadmap or accepted decomposition mentions G-rings or the ascent of formal fibres, and the libraries have no excellence. PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23/Z79 is missing; its route 7 goes to SF.0, SF.1, SF.4 and SF.5, and that extraction is partial with no review, so nothing there is accepted. The red team missed that accepted routes already give R03.3 special cases of the regular case. These are BOCKLE-IYENGAR-PASKUNAS-23/088 (route 1) and PASKUNAS-QUAST-26/76 (route 3): finitely generated algebras over complete local Noetherian rings are excellent. KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/60 has finitely generated O-algebras excellent, planned in R03.3. CLAUSEN-MATHEW-MORROW-21/080 is on route 5, whose review says 'R03.3 is where excellence … lives'. Item 1's own note puts ring-level excellence in R03.3 and cites the first two. Those special cases are proved through the G-ring ascent along finite type (Stacks 07PV), so R03.3 is already committed to the regular case. Putting the general theorem on route 1, as the fix says, would plan it twice. Right fix: add the item in ring form, on route 4 as a source of R03.3. Statement: if the local rings of a Noetherian ring A have formal fibres with P, P ∈ {geometrically regular, Cohen–Macaulay, (S_n)} under the axioms of EGA IV₂ 7.3 (7.3.8), then so do those of every finitely generated A-algebra and its localisations (EGA IV₂ 7.4.4; Stacks 07PV for G-rings). Corollary: finite-type algebras over quasi-excellent rings are quasi-excellent (7.8.3(ii)). BIP-23/088 and PQ-26/76 then become special cases of it. Cite it from items 1, 6, 25 and 28. Items 6 and 28 stay on route 1, together with the open-subscheme condition from EGA IV₂ 6.11.9(i). Add to item 25 (or item 1) the clause that quasi-excellence passes to finite (and finite-type) X-schemes. Route 1's brief should import the item from R03.3. Note for the maintainer: when LLL-23 is reviewed, point Z79 to this R03.3 item rather than to SF.

Confirmed; one detail of the claim is slightly off. At TeX l. 1533 the proof of Theorem 3.14 identifies the support of Bl_I(M) with the blowing up of Supp(M) and bounds its dimension by dim Supp(M), citing HIO 12.14. It then uses that Cohen–Macaulayness is stable under localisation to reduce to depth ≥ dim Supp(M) at the closed points. Item 49's statement does mention this bound as a cited step, so it is not 'only in the list of references'. But no item states it and no supplier is named. Of the five HIO results the extraction's prerequisites list as used and not reproved, 12.14 is the only one without an item: 14.11 is item 50, and 18.17, 18.20/18.26 and 38.6 b) have items. I read StableReduction Layer 4 in full (Rees algebra, universal property, projectivity, flat base change, exceptional divisor, strict transform, charts): it has no dimension clause. R03.3 says only 'depth and dimension formulas under the local maps actually used'. Its accepted decomposition's one dimension node (depth, Auslander–Buchsbaum and dimension bounds) says nothing about Rees algebras or blowups. R09.7a builds blowups by the Rees algebra but states no dimension either. No extraction item plans it. Mathlib at 082e2d3 has reesAlgebra and reesAlgebra.fg, and dim R[X] = dim R + 1 for Noetherian R, but nothing for R[It] or for Proj. I checked the mathematics. Put A = R/Ann(M) and S = A[IAt]; then Supp(Bl_I(M)) = Proj S. Given a chain P_0 ⊊ … ⊊ P_k of homogeneous primes not containing S_+, the prime (P_k ∩ A) ⊕ S_+ properly contains P_k, so dim Proj S ≤ dim S − 1. Also dim S ≤ dim A + 1: every minimal prime of S is the contraction of a minimal prime q of A, and (A/q)[It] is a domain of transcendence degree at most 1 over A/q, so the dimension inequality for finitely generated extensions of Noetherian domains applies. Hence dim Bl ≤ dim Supp(M). Neither step is routine or in the libraries. The fix is right. Add to it the Proj step and the dimension inequality behind dim R[It] ≤ dim R + 1. The ring-level Rees bound has other potential consumers (the blowups of StableReduction Layer 4 and of R09.7a). So it can equally go on route 4 as a source of R03.3, with the blowup corollary on route 2; either placement is acceptable.

I fetched the author's file myself. Its SHA-256 is 55ded201…9ac6, which matches the recorded hash. The PDF metadata give CreationDate and ModDate D:20200728101622+02'00' (08:16 UTC on 28 July 2020), producer pdfTeX-1.40.18 (TeX Live 2017) and creator 'LaTeX with hyperref'. The file has 24 pages. Page 1 reads 'Date: July 28, 2020', with the author's Orsay address, in the author's own amsart layout, not Duke's typesetting. arXiv v2 was submitted on 3 September 2020; its TeX has \date{\today}, and its PDF prints September 4, 2020. The Duke article, 170 (2021), no. 7, pp. 1419–1455, is 37 pages. Crossref gives print publication on 5 May 2021 and registers no correction. The DOI redirects to Project Euclid, which returned an Incapsula 'Request unsuccessful' page to scripted requests, including for the download link Crossref lists. OpenAlex lists the Duke version as closed, with no open copy, and its HAL entry links to arXiv. The author's page lists the Duke reference and no corrigendum. So nobody read the version of record. Yet readSections calls the file 'the author's copy of the published version'. The report's E1 bullet speaks of 'the content stream of the published PDF'. Every locator of E1–E9 gives pages 'of the author's copy of the published version', and E3's 'searched' entry says 'in the published version … the two texts agree'. The review writes that 'the published and arXiv texts … are the same'. There is no sourceVersions field. The fix is right except for one step. Relabel the file 'the author's manuscript dated 28 July 2020, listed under the Duke reference'. Add sourceVersions entries: kind 'author copy' for that file (URL, read 2026-09-23, hash), and kind 'preprint' for arXiv v2 (e-print and PDF, with both hashes). Note that the Duke text was not read because Project Euclid refuses automated access. Rescope E1–E9 to these two texts: 'known: new' then means new relative to them, and page numbers are the manuscript's, not Duke's. The step 'add the paper to REQUESTS.md' does not work. That file is generated by the collation script's write option. It lists only papers with a finding whose 'affects' is 'a stated result', and the collation-job generator uses the same test. E1–E8 have 'nothing' and E9 has 'the proof', so a hand edit would disappear at the next regeneration. Instead, record for the maintainer that the Duke text is unread. It should be collated by someone with browser access, above all for E1 (the printed statement of Corollary 1.11) and E2 (§1.13).
